newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria depo rates ease on higher bank liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria depo rates ease on higher bank liquidity.

text.p: Bulgaria's interbank deposit rates eased on Tuesday amid low demand for lev funds as banks' liquidity rose on government securities maturity payment, dealers said.
Banks received around 16.5 billion levs interest and principal on a treasury bill issue on Tuesday, Finance Ministry figures showed.
Depo rates for overnight to three-day depos were 1.3-1.5 percent annually against 1.3-1.9 percent on Monday and one-week deposits traded at 1.7-2.0 percent annually against 1.8-2.75.

But interest rates on two-week to one-month deposits stood at 3.0-3.5 percent annually, up from Monday's 2.7-3.0 percent due to the market expectations of a further rise in the central bank main interest rate.
The main rate has steadily risen in the past four weeks weeks to 5.70 percent annually now from 5.42 percent in the week to August 1.

Dealers expected the central bank to raise the main rate to around 5.86 percent from next week in line with rising yield to maturity of the benchmark three-month discount T-bills sold by the Finance Ministry each Monday.
The average yield to maturity of the three-month paper sold on Monday rose to 1.46 percent from 1.42 percent a week earlier.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 1.98 percent on Monday, higher than 1.55 percent on Friday, a central bank official said.

There was one final sale of dollar-denominated government bonds known as ZUNKs with a par value of $2,200 at 76 percent of par and 12 repo deals for a total par of 22.973 billion levs on the secondary interbank market of government securities on Monday.
